'''Guillermo Vargas Aignasse''' (born in 1943, disappeared 1976) was an [[Argentines|Argentine]] [[Peronism|Peronist]] politician, serving as a provincial Senator in [[Tucumán Province]] from 1973 until his [[Desaparecidos|disappearance]] in 1976. In 2008, two former generals were jailed for life for his disappearance.<ref name=bbc>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/americas/7587199.stm Argentine chiefs jailed for life], [[BBC Online]], 28 August 2008.</ref>

==Background==
Vargas Aignasse was born and raised in [[Andalgalá]], [[Catamarca Province]], and was a [[physicist]] by profession, teaching in the discipline until his election to the Provincial Senate of Tucumán in 1973. He was elected on the [[Justicialist Party|Frejuli]] ticket that brought [[Peronist]]s back to power, and was associated with the left-wing faction of Peronism, having belonged to the center-left FANE (National Student Associations Front).<ref name=pagina12>[http://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/elpais/1-109199-2008-08-07.html ''Página/12'': Hay muchos fantasmas que lo abruman] {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[http://www.diariodecuyo.com.ar/home/new_noticia.php?noticia_id=129880 ''Diario del Cuyo'': Guardia de Hierro del PJ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719014815/http://www.diariodecuyo.com.ar/home/new_noticia.php?noticia_id=129880 |date=2011-07-19 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref> Amid the worst climate of violence in the country, Tucumán Province was placed under [[martial law]] in January 1975, after which [[Operativo Independencia]], a [[counterinsurgency]] offensive, was launched by presidential order. The installation of General [[Antonio Domingo Bussi]] as its commander in December coincided with Vargas Aignasse's investigation of provincial Police Chief Colonel Antonio Arrechea on reports of [[drug trafficking]].<ref name=pagina12/>

The [[1976 Argentine coup d'état|1976 military coup]], on March 24, resulted in Vargas Aignasse's arrest by provincial police, who had their detainee turn in all documentation regarding the Arrechea case. Days later, his brother, Rodolfo, was allowed to see the prisoner from above a patio, following which, per police testimony, he was released from prison on 5 April and 'kidnapped by parties unknown' while being taken home in an official car. He was later reportedly seen alive and in pain by a number of witnesses, though his whereabouts afterwards remained unknown.<ref name=pagina12/>

Unable to do so until after the [[1983 Argentine general election|return of democracy]] in 1983, Rodolfo Vargas Aignasse filed a missing persons case on February 6, 1984. Ultimately, and despite the unwillingness of numerous witnesses to testify, Bussi was arrested for ordering Vargas Aignasse's abduction, on October 15, 2003.<ref name=appeals>Dictamen de procesamiento de [http://www.nuncamas.org/juicios/argentin/tucuman/tucuman_15dic04.htm Indictment of Generals Antonio Domingo Bussi and Luciano Benjamín Menéndez, Federal Appeals Court of Tucumán] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071009002541/http://www.nuncamas.org/juicios/argentin/tucuman/tucuman_15dic04.htm |date=2007-10-09 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref> During the trial that formally began in July 2008, former trade union leader Juan Antonio Palavecino testified that he had seen Vargas Aignasse in Tucumán police headquarters showing signs of torture on April 6, 1976, one day after his supposed kidnapping, and contrary to the official story.<ref name=clarin>{{in lang|es}} [http://www.clarin.com/diario/2008/08/29/um/m-01748210.htm Condenan a perpetua a Bussi y a Menéndez por una desaparición] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080912142653/http://www.clarin.com/diario/2008/08/29/um/m-01748210.htm |date=2008-09-12 }}, ''[[Clarín (Argentine newspaper)|Clarín]]'', 28 August 2008.</ref> Bussi and former General [[Luciano Benjamín Menéndez]] were found guilty of Vargas Aignasse's [[forced disappearance]] and sentenced to [[life imprisonment]] on August 28.<ref name=clarin/>

[[Rodolfo Vargas Aignasse]] was elected to the [[Argentine Chamber of Deputies]] in 1987, and the disappeared lawmaker's son, [[Gerónimo Vargas Aignasse]], is currently a member of the Chamber.
